topStories.headline: Autumn Moon Festival Takes Over Irving Street Tonight as Sunset Night Market Returns
topStories.dek: Five blocks of Irving Street close to traffic this evening for the third Sunset Night Market of 2026, timed to coincide with the Mid-Autumn Festival.
topStories.body:
Irving Street between 19th and 26th Avenues will be closed to vehicles from noon through midnight tonight, Friday, September 25, as the Sunset Night Market: Autumn Moon Festival runs from 5 to 10 p.m. The SFMTA confirmed the closure in its weekly traffic advisory published September 24, noting that the intersections at 20th and 25th Avenues will remain open and that Muni service will not be affected.

The event, presented by Sunset Mercantile in partnership with Wah Mei School, Into The Streets, and ASIAN Inc., is the third in a four-part 2026 series. This edition is timed to the Mid-Autumn Festival — which falls on September 25 this year — a harvest celebration marked across East and Southeast Asian cultures with mooncakes, lanterns, family gatherings, and music. Attendees can expect food vendors, live entertainment, cultural performances, artisan goods, and interactive activities along the car-free corridor.

The Sunset Chinese Cultural District co-presents the event and notes that the night market also launches the 'Taste of Sunset' season: attendees can purchase a $5 voucher redeemable for $10 in value at participating local restaurants through October 16. Organizers recommend arriving by public transit — Muni lines 7, 29, 28, 91, and the N Judah all serve the corridor — and note that bike valet will be available on-site. Street parking in the area will be extremely limited during the closure.

The series started in 2023 spanning three blocks of Irving Street and has grown steadily since. The fourth and final night market of the year is scheduled for December 11.

topStories.headline: Neighbors Challenge Flaws in St. Ignatius Field Lighting Environmental Report
topStories.dek: The St. Ignatius Neighborhood Association has filed written objections to a court-ordered draft EIR for the school's 90-foot stadium lights, calling the analysis riddled with errors.
topStories.body:
Residents living around St. Ignatius College Preparatory School on 37th Avenue in the Outer Sunset have formally responded to a Draft Environmental Impact Report published by the San Francisco Planning Department, arguing that the document contains significant factual errors and flawed analysis, according to a report published September 19 by the Sunset Beacon.

The dispute dates to 2018, when St. Ignatius proposed installing four 90-foot LED light standards at J.B. Murphy Field to allow evening athletic events. After the Planning Department initially ruled the project exempt from California Environmental Quality Act review, the St. Ignatius Neighborhood Association (SINA) pursued litigation. A Superior Court ultimately ordered the city to prepare a full EIR — the document now under public scrutiny.

The Draft EIR, filed with the state CEQA clearinghouse in May 2026, proposes allowing field lights on up to 135 evenings per school year, with some events extending to 10 p.m. The DEIR concluded that impacts would be 'less than significant.' In their written response, SINA contends the baseline conditions used in the report are incorrect or mischaracterized, that stated event counts are internally inconsistent, and that the analysis treats permanent nightly lighting impacts as temporary. The association urged the Planning Commission to require a more thorough biological resources and noise analysis before certifying the document.

The lights were physically installed in November 2021 and have been operating under a court-supervised interim agreement with SINA while the EIR process proceeds. The Planning Commission must certify the final EIR and approve a conditional use authorization before the school can operate the lights under a permanent program.

topStories.headline: 39 Days to the Vote: Great Highway Debate Heats Up as November Ballot Nears
topStories.dek: With Proposition G on the November 3 ballot, the fight over whether to reopen the Upper Great Highway to weekday car traffic is entering its final stretch.
topStories.body:
San Francisco voters will decide on November 3 whether to partially reopen the Upper Great Highway — now the Sunset Dunes park — to private vehicles on weekdays. Supporters of Proposition G gathered more than 15,900 signatures to qualify the measure, which was certified by the Department of Elections on July 23. The measure would allow cars on the two-mile stretch Monday through Friday while keeping it closed on weekends and holidays, reversing the 2024 Proposition K that permanently closed the road.

The Richmond Review published additional commentary on the measure on September 22, reflecting continued strong community interest in the Sunset District, where the highway forms the western edge of the neighborhood. The Controller's Office has estimated that reopening the road would require approximately $9.8 million in one-time capital costs — mostly for reinstalling traffic signals at eight intersections — plus $500,000 to $1.9 million in ongoing annual costs. A separate SFMTA/Rec and Parks analysis put removal of existing park features at an additional $14 million.

Opponents, including Friends of Sunset Dunes president Lucas Lux and a majority of the Board of Supervisors, argue that weekday use represents 60 percent of park visits and that the measure would effectively destroy the park. Supervisor Alan Wong, who represents District 4 and succeeded the recalled Joel Engardio, has publicly backed the initiative. Prop G needs a simple majority to pass.

events.title: Sunset Night Market: Autumn Moon Festival
events.location: Irving Street between 19th and 26th Avenues, Inner Sunset
events.description: Free, all-ages night market with food vendors, live entertainment, cultural performances, lanterns, and mooncakes to mark the Mid-Autumn Festival. Bike valet available; Muni lines 7, 28, 29, 91, and N serve the corridor.

events.title: Bodhi Mid-Autumn Festival Community Fair
events.location: San Francisco County Fair Building, 1199 9th Ave (Golden Gate Park)
events.description: Free community fair presented by Bodhi Meditation San Francisco featuring lantern displays, Hanfu experiences, multicultural performances, crafts, games, and a photo booth. All ages welcome.

events.title: Inner Sunset Farmers' Market
events.location: 1315 8th Ave (parking lot between 8th and 9th Ave off Irving), Inner Sunset
events.description: Year-round Sunday farmers market operated by the Pacific Coast Farmers' Market Association, with seasonal produce, honey, eggs, artisan cheese, and other local goods.

events.title: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass 2026
events.time: 1:00 PM–7:00 PM Fri; 9:00 AM–7:00 PM Sat–Sun
events.location: Hellman Hollow, Lindley & Marx Meadows, Golden Gate Park
events.description: The 26th annual free music festival returns to Golden Gate Park with 71 concerts across six stages over three days. Artists include Robert Plant with Saving Grace, Rilo Kiley, Gillian Welch & David Rawlings, My Morning Jacket, and Old Crow Medicine Show, among dozens more.

events.title: Secondhand Saturday Vintage Market — Outer Sunset
events.date: Saturday, October 18 (third Saturday monthly through November)
events.location: 37th Avenue between Ortega and Quintara Streets, Outer Sunset / Parkside
events.description: Monthly free vintage and makers market organized by Sunset Mercantile, featuring over 60 vendors, live music, food trucks, and family-friendly activities. October's edition honors Halloween, Día de los Muertos, and Diwali.

events.title: Inner Sunset Flea Market (Second Sundays)
events.location: Irving Street between 9th and 11th Avenues, Inner Sunset
events.description: Monthly street flea market in its 11th season, presented by Sunset Mercantile in collaboration with Inner Sunset Park Neighbors. The next date is Sunday, October 11.

moreNews.headline: Abanico Coffee Roasters Plans Irving Street Opening
moreNews.body: Abanico Coffee Roasters announced via social media that it is preparing to open a café and roasting operation at 424 Irving St. in the Inner Sunset, according to a report published September 19, 2026, by Whatnow San Francisco. The new shop would add another locally-focused coffee destination to the Inner Sunset's Irving Street commercial corridor. No opening date has been publicly announced.

moreNews.headline: Irving Street Closed Between 19th and 26th Avenues Tonight for Night Market
moreNews.body: The SFMTA's September 24 weekly traffic advisory confirms that Irving Street between 19th and 26th Avenues will be closed to through traffic from noon to 11:59 p.m. on Friday, September 25, to accommodate the Sunset Night Market. Intersections at 20th and 25th Avenues will remain open, and local access only will be permitted on 22nd and 23rd Avenues between Lincoln Way and Judah Street. No Muni service impacts are expected.

restaurants.name: Outerlands
restaurants.type: Organic farm-to-table café and dinner restaurant
restaurants.description: Beloved Outer Sunset gathering place serving locally sourced, organic fare — famous for house-baked sourdough, Dutch baby pancakes, and seasonal dinner dishes in a warm, handcrafted space.

restaurants.name: San Tung
restaurants.description: Inner Sunset institution since 1986, legendary for its dry-fried chicken wings and handmade dumplings, drawing long lines at both lunch and dinner.

restaurants.name: Hook Fish
restaurants.description: Hook-and-line-sourced seafood restaurant and market near Ocean Beach, known for fresh fish tacos, poke, and ceviche with an emphasis on transparent, local sourcing.

restaurants.name: Fifty Vara
restaurants.description: Neighborhood kitchen and bar on Noriega Street with a menu rooted in the Outer Sunset — brunch, lunch, and dinner with a kids menu and a quintessentially local feel.

restaurants.name: Maillards Smash Burgers
restaurants.description: Farmers-market favorite turned permanent restaurant, sharing space with Two Pitchers Brewing on Noriega — serving smashburgers, fries, sandwiches, and soft serve.

restaurants.name: Two Pitchers Brewing
restaurants.description: Outer Sunset brewpub sharing its Noriega Street space with Maillards, pouring house lagers, radlers, and a rotating tap list Wednesday through Sunday.

restaurants.name: Elena's
restaurants.description: Buzzy West Portal Mexican restaurant from the Duggan family (Original Joe's), featuring copper booths, Mexican-made tableware, and a full bar.

restaurants.name: Little Original Joe's
restaurants.description: West Portal specialty market and takeout spot from the Original Joe's family — rotisserie chicken, specialty pizza, pasta, and the smash burger that inspired their next concept.

restaurants.name: Andytown Coffee Roasters
restaurants.description: Irish-influenced Outer Sunset original since 2014, roasting its own beans and baking all pastries in-house; famous for the Snowy Plover (espresso, sparkling water, whipped cream) and a perpetual line out the door.

restaurants.name: Snowbird Coffee
restaurants.description: Inner Sunset's beloved pour-over café tucked near 9th and Irving, roasting its own single-origin beans and offering a quiet, knowledgeable coffee experience.

restaurants.name: Arizmendi Bakery
restaurants.description: Beloved worker-owned co-op on 9th Avenue renowned for freshly baked sourdough, daily pizza slices, scones, and pecan rolls — almost always with a line.

restaurants.name: The Riptide
restaurants.description: Laid-back Outer Sunset bar on Taraval Street with a fireplace, pool table, and a packed calendar of free live music acts ranging from country to rock.

restaurants.name: Sunset Cantina
restaurants.description: Outer Sunset neighborhood Mexican bar and restaurant on Judah Street near the beach, known for generous tacos, margaritas, and a welcoming local crowd.

restaurants.name: Tadaima
restaurants.description: Matcha-focused café from the Japantown brand, opened at 1248 9th Avenue in early 2026 and quickly embraced by Inner Sunset regulars.

restaurants.name: The Beanery
restaurants.description: Classic Inner Sunset coffeehouse serving hot and cold drinks brewed with 100% Arabica beans, with locations on Irving Street and 9th Avenue.

hotels.name: Ocean Park Motel
hotels.description: Family-run 1937 Art Deco 'Streamlined Moderne' motel one block from Ocean Beach and the San Francisco Zoo, featuring porthole windows, an outdoor hot tub, garden play area, and kitchenette rooms.

hotels.name: The SeaScape Inn
hotels.description: Simple, affordable motel within five minutes' walk of Ocean Beach and Golden Gate Park, offering ocean views, free parking, and basic amenities.

hotels.name: Ocean Inn
hotels.description: Classic 1950s surf-vibes motel in the Outer Sunset with a microwave and fridge in every room, one block from Golden Gate Park and five minutes' walk from Ocean Beach; the on-site Pittsburg Pub is a neighborhood hangout.

shops.name: Green Apple Books on the Park
shops.description: Inner Sunset branch of San Francisco's legendary Green Apple Books, situated just outside Golden Gate Park with an extensive selection of new titles, handwritten staff picks, and author events; the upstairs mezzanine is now home to the Backstory Above literary co-working space.

shops.name: Amazing Fantasy Comics
shops.description: Irving Street institution under current owner Frank McGinn since August 2000, carrying new comics, back issues, graphic novels, and collectibles for fans of all ages.

shops.name: Stonestown Galleria
shops.description: Western San Francisco's major indoor shopping center anchoring the Stonestown neighborhood, with major retailers, dining options, and a Trader Joe's; redevelopment plans call for thousands of new housing units on surrounding parking lots.

shops.name: Therapy Stores
shops.description: Local San Francisco gift shop chain, with a 9th and Irving location opened in early 2026 marking the brand's first push onto the west side.

shops.name: Other Avenues Food Co-op
shops.description: Community-owned natural food cooperative in the Outer Sunset carrying organic produce, bulk foods, supplements, and local products since 1974.

shops.name: Sunset Gym
shops.description: Well-equipped, no-frills neighborhood fitness center on 9th Avenue open daily with cardio, free weights, and a friendly community atmosphere.

shops.name: San Franpsycho
shops.description: Homegrown San Francisco streetwear brand with an Inner Sunset flagship celebrating west-side culture through apparel, art prints, and accessories.

artEntertainment.name: Marrow Gallery
artEntertainment.description: Inner Sunset community-focused gallery at 7th and Irving showing local, national, and international artists with monthly rotating exhibitions; open Wednesday through Sunday.

artEntertainment.name: Problem Library
artEntertainment.description: Experimental Inner Sunset art and education space at 1288 15th Ave. that also hosts a residency program connecting artists with vacant commercial storefronts across the city.

artEntertainment.name: Great Highway Gallery
artEntertainment.description: Outer Sunset gallery on Lawton Street anchoring the neighborhood's arts community since 2013, championing local artists near Ocean Beach.

artEntertainment.name: Birdhouse Gallery
artEntertainment.description: Small Outer Sunset gallery at Judah and 31st Avenue run by local architect Ben Frombgen, presenting work in an intimate neighborhood setting.

artEntertainment.name: Sunset Dunes Park
artEntertainment.type: Oceanfront linear park and public space
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's newest and largest park — a two-mile promenade along the former Upper Great Highway between Lincoln Way and Sloat Boulevard — hosting free fitness classes, community events, and public art year-round.
artEntertainment.address: Great Highway between Lincoln Way and Sloat Blvd

artEntertainment.name: Golden Gate Park
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's iconic 1,017-acre park bordering the Inner Sunset, encompassing the de Young Museum, California Academy of Sciences, Japanese Tea Garden, Botanical Garden, free summer concerts, and miles of trails.

artEntertainment.name: The Riptide
artEntertainment.description: Outer Sunset live-music institution on Taraval offering free shows nearly every night in a cozy, fireplace-warmed setting.

artEntertainment.name: Sunset Recreation Center
artEntertainment.description: Bustling SF Rec & Parks community center in the Outer Sunset with basketball, tennis, baseball, after-school programs, dance classes, and one of the city's most popular table tennis rooms.

gymsRecreation.name: Sunset Gym
gymsRecreation.description: Affordable, well-appointed neighborhood gym on 9th Avenue with cardio equipment, free weights, and a welcoming community feel; open daily from 6 AM.

gymsRecreation.name: Sunset Recreation Center Gymnasium
gymsRecreation.description: SF Rec & Parks facility offering drop-in basketball, table tennis, zumba, hatha yoga, and after-school programming in the Outer Sunset.

gymsRecreation.name: Sunset Dunes Park (Free Fitness Programs)
gymsRecreation.type: Oceanfront park with free fitness programming
gymsRecreation.description: The two-mile Sunset Dunes promenade hosts free recurring fitness classes including Zumba, chair yoga, and Cantonese-language dance for seniors, plus regular community cleanups and events.
gymsRecreation.address: Great Highway between Lincoln Way and Sloat Blvd

gymsRecreation.name: Golden Gate Park — Polo Field Cycling Track
gymsRecreation.description: Free-access oval cycling and running track inside Golden Gate Park, regularly used by cyclists, joggers, and inline skaters of all levels.
gymsRecreation.address: Golden Gate Park, near Fulton St & 38th Ave

gymsRecreation.name: Lake Merced Park
gymsRecreation.description: 614-acre park adjacent to Parkmerced offering miles of recreational trails around a freshwater lake used for fishing, rowing, and bird-watching.
gymsRecreation.address: Lake Merced Blvd at Sunset Blvd

gymsRecreation.name: TPC Harding Park
gymsRecreation.description: Championship-caliber municipal golf course adjacent to Lake Merced, hosting PGA Tour events and open to the public with accessible tee times.

gymsRecreation.name: Stern Grove
gymsRecreation.description: Beloved eucalyptus grove hosting the city's longest-running free outdoor concert series each summer, surrounded by walking paths and picnic areas.

gymsRecreation.name: San Francisco Zoo
gymsRecreation.description: Oceanside zoo at the western edge of the Sunset, home to more than 2,000 animals with regular family programming and special exhibits year-round.

gymsRecreation.name: Ocean Beach
gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's widest public beach, stretching four miles along the western edge of the Sunset; popular with surfers, joggers, kite flyers, and bonfire-permit holders at designated spots.
